title: What is Realistic Fiction Genre?
use_cases: Use when defining literary genres in a curriculum or database
Implement when categorizing fiction manuscripts based on narrative elements
Configure when establishing criteria for non-speculative creative writing projects
Use when distinguishing grounded narratives from fantasy or science fiction
content:
This section examines core features of the genre and how it is distinguished from other types of fiction.

Key attributes of realistic fiction include:

- A setting that seems like it could actually happen or could exist in real life.
- Characters who behave like people we might meet, facing plausible conflicts such as job loss, love, family tension, coming of age.
- A plot anchored in everyday life, rather than fantastical or speculative environments.
- Absence of overt magical or supernatural elements; the world resembles ours.
